answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with work-backed, non-transferable identity: each agent earns one credential by completing audited tasks verified by peers, like a quill that writes after its pigment is ground by hand. One fake identity is cheap to claim, but a thousand fakes cost a thousand rounds of real work, while a relic of past fraud, an immutable record of revoked credentials, lets the network reject repeat offenders at near-zero cost. The attacker cost scales linearly with every fake, while an honest agent pays once.
